title: A Call Across the Bus: Requests, Responses, Timeouts and the Command That Ran Twice

questions.question: A call gets no answer. What can the caller conclude?
options: Nothing: the request may not have arrived, or may have been done with the answer lost, or the answer may be late

questions.question: Why does each call carry a number?
options: So an answer is matched to the call it answers: two calls answered in the other order each got their own answer
questions.explanation: Whichever is waiting is the wrong match.

questions.question: A call timed out and its answer arrives. What happens?
options: The answer is unwanted: counted and discarded, and the call stays timed out
questions.explanation: A late answer does not revive a call.

questions.question: With no retries, 155 of 300 calls timed out. How many times did the work run?
options: 214: for 69 calls the work was done and the client was told it had failed
questions.explanation: A timeout is not a failure, it is not knowing.

questions.question: What keeps a retried call from doing the work twice?
options: A server that remembers the answers it gave by (client, number) and returns the remembered one for a repeat: 300 runs for 300 calls, against 446 for a server that forgot
questions.explanation: Retrying is safe only if asking again does not do it again.

questions.question: Why is a repeated gripper command harmless and a repeated dispense command not?
options: The gripper closing twice leaves it closed, and dispensing twice gives two: the first is idempotent and the second is not, so the second needs the server to remember
questions.explanation: Know which of your services are safe to repeat.
